questions.question: Which Procurement view widget shows the count of purchase orders that aren't received and aren't canceled?

explanation.correct: The 'Purchase order pending delivery' widget shows the count of purchase orders that aren't received and aren't canceled. Only purchase orders with status of Requested, Ordered, or Pending Delivery are displayed.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Expenditure by vendor shows the cost paid to each vendor for procuring inventory.
Requests pending approval shows sourceable and active requests with pending approval status.
Open purchase orders shows requested, ordered, or not delivered purchase orders as a list, not just pending delivery count.

source.excerpt: Purchase order pending delivery: Count of purchase orders that aren't received and aren't canceled. Only purchase orders that have a status of Requested, Ordered, or Pending Delivery are displayed.

questions.question: Which filters are available in the Procurement view of the Hardware Asset Workspace? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: You can use Location, Stockroom, and Domain filters in the Procurement view to narrow down your results. Note: The Domain filter is available only when Domain Extensions Installer and Domain Separation plugins are enabled.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Vendor is not listed as a filter option in the Procurement view.
Model category is a filter in Hardware asset overview, but not mentioned for Procurement view.

source.excerpt: You can also use Location, Stockroom, and Domain filters to narrow down your results.

questions.question: Which plugins must be enabled for the Domain filter to appear in the Procurement view?

options.text: Domain Extensions Installer and Domain Separation
Hardware Asset Management and Domain Separation

explanation.correct: The Domain filter is available only when you've enabled the Domain Extensions Installer (com.glide.domain.msp_extensions.installer) and Domain Separation (plugin com.snc.pa.domain_support) plugins.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Domain Separation alone is not sufficient; Domain Extensions Installer is also required.
The correct plugin names are Domain Extensions Installer and Domain Separation.
HAM is a prerequisite but the Domain filter specifically requires Domain Extensions Installer and Domain Separation.

source.excerpt: The Domain filter is available only when you've enabled the Domain Extensions Installer (com.glide.domain.msp_extensions.installer) and Domain Separation (plugin com.snc.pa.domain_support) plugins.

questions.question: Which Procurement view widget shows requests for which a purchase order, local order, or transfer order hasn't been initiated?

options.text: Requests by state for last 30 days

explanation.correct: The 'Requests that require sourcing' widget shows a list of requests for which a purchase order, local order, or transfer order hasn't been initiated.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Requests pending approval shows sourceable and active requests with request state of pending approval.
Requests by state shows requests created in last 30 days grouped by state.
Open purchase orders shows purchase orders that have been requested, ordered, or not delivered.

source.excerpt: Requests that require sourcing: List of requests for which a purchase order, local order, or transfer order hasn't been initiated.

questions.question: Which inventory report helps identify suitable replacement options for assets that are in use, in maintenance, pending repair, or defective?

explanation.correct: The Inventory availability report is used to determine suitable replacement options for assets and their child components that are in use, in maintenance, pending repair, or defective.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Supply vs Demand report evaluates available and incoming quantity of models and requests for them.
Open demands report determines available stock within local stockrooms and distribution channels to fulfill sourcing requests.
Stockroom inventory report is not the specific name; the correct report is Inventory availability report.

references: Manage stockrooms with inventory reports in the Hardware Asset Workspace

source.excerpt: Use the Inventory availability report to determine suitable replacement options for your assets and their child components that are in use, in maintenance, pending repair, or defective.

questions.question: What information does the Inventory availability report help determine? (Choose two.)

options.text: Quantity of available substitute models locally
Total cost of ownership for assets
Estimated lead time for new purchases

explanation.correct: The Inventory availability report helps determine the quantity of available substitute models that can be used locally, moved through distribution channels, and estimate the lead time for new purchases.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Total cost of ownership is calculated separately through the TCO feature, not the Inventory availability report.
Depreciation is calculated by the Calculate Depreciation scheduled job, not inventory reports.

references: Manage stockrooms with inventory reports in the Hardware Asset Workspace

source.excerpt: The report also helps you to determine the quantity of available substitute models that can be used locally, moved through the distribution channels, and estimate the lead time for new purchases.

questions.question: Which HAM version is required to access the inventory reports feature?

options.text: Hardware Asset Management version 10.0.0 or later
Hardware Asset Management version 11.0.0 or later
Hardware Asset Management version 12.0.0 or later
Hardware Asset Management version 13.0.0 or later

explanation.correct: The inventory reports are available with Hardware Asset Management version 13.0.0 and later.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Version 10.0.0 introduced Asset TCO, but inventory reports require version 13.0.0.
Version 11.0.0 is not the minimum version for inventory reports.
Version 12.0.0 is not the minimum version for inventory reports.

references: Manage stockrooms with inventory reports in the Hardware Asset Workspace

source.excerpt: Important: The inventory reports are available with Hardware Asset Management version 13.0.0 and later.

questions.question: Which report helps you determine if you have enough assets to meet demand by evaluating available and incoming quantity of models in your stockroom?

options.text: Asset count by lifecycle state report

explanation.correct: The Supply vs Demand report evaluates the available and incoming quantity of models in your stockroom and the requests for these models from different service locations. This report helps you determine if you have enough assets to meet the demand.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Inventory availability report is for finding replacement options for assets in various states.
Open demands report determines available stock to fulfill sourcing requests that are open.
Asset count by lifecycle state is part of the 360 asset view, not a stockroom demand report.

references: Manage stockrooms with inventory reports in the Hardware Asset Workspace

source.excerpt: Use the Supply vs Demand report to evaluate the available and incoming quantity of models in your stockroom and the requests for these models from different service locations. This report helps you determine if you have enough assets to meet the demand.

questions.question: An asset manager needs to find available stock to fulfill open sourcing requests. Which report should they use?

explanation.correct: The Open demands report is used to determine available stock within local stockrooms and distribution channels to fulfill sourcing requests that are open.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Inventory availability report is for finding replacement options, not fulfilling open sourcing requests.
Supply vs Demand evaluates supply levels versus demand, but Open demands specifically addresses open sourcing requests.
Requests that require sourcing is a Procurement view widget, not an inventory report.

references: Manage stockrooms with inventory reports in the Hardware Asset Workspace

source.excerpt: Use the Open demands report to determine available stock within local stockrooms and distribution channels to fulfill sourcing requests that are open.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the Hardware asset overview are true?
a) The 360 asset view shows asset counts by model category and lifecycle state.
b) The Overall performance section displays discovered and undiscovered asset count.
c) The Model normalization widget shows the total number of models.
d) The Hardware asset overview supports lazy loading of reports.

explanation.correct: Statement c is false - the Model normalization widget shows the PERCENTAGE of hardware and consumable models that are normalized, not the total number. Statements a, b, and d are all true.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement c is false - Model normalization shows percentage, not total count.
Statement d is also true - lazy loading is supported via system property.
Statement c is false - it shows percentage, not count.

source.excerpt: Model normalization: Percentage of hardware and consumable models that are normalized. 360 asset view: Asset counts by model category and lifecycle state. Overall performance: Discovered and undiscovered asset count.

questions.question: Which Hardware asset overview widget shows assets that have already expired or are on the expiry date and are eligible for a refresh?

options.text: Assets eligible for refresh by model category

explanation.correct: The 'Assets eligible for refresh by model category' widget shows the number of assets that have already expired or the current day is the expiry date, and are eligible for a refresh.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Model lifecycle overview shows the overview of model lifecycle grouped by lifecycle phase like End of support, End of Life, etc.
Asset count by lifecycle state shows assets grouped by state like Retired, In use, In stock.
Refresh requests shows the number of open hardware assets refresh order requests, not eligibility.

source.excerpt: Assets eligible for refresh by model category: Number of assets that have already expired or the current day is the expiry date, and are eligible for a refresh.

questions.question: Which subscription unit ratio applies to Mobile Devices in the HAM licensing model?

explanation.correct: Mobile Devices have a subscription unit ratio of 10:1, meaning 10 mobile device assets require 1 subscription unit.

wrongAnswers.explanation: 4:1 is the ratio for End User Computers, not Mobile Devices.
5:1 is the ratio for Network Gear, not Mobile Devices.
15:1 is the ratio for Monitors, not Mobile Devices.

questions.question: What system property controls whether HAM licensing applies to custom model categories?

explanation.correct: The sn_hamp.enable_custom_category_licensing property (default false) controls whether HAM licensing applies to custom model categories. When true, custom model category assets are excluded from HAM workflows unless their parent is an opted-in licensable category.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This property stores HAM entitlement details for on-premise instances, not custom category licensing.
This property controls async asset creation from CIs, unrelated to licensing.
This property enables CI creation using IRE, not related to custom category licensing.

questions.question: An organization has an on-premise ServiceNow instance. How should they store their HAM entitlement details?

options.text: Upload an entitlement file to the Asset Management module
Update the sn_ham_active_entitlements system property with a comma-separated list of entitlements
Create entitlement records in the Software Entitlement table
Contact ServiceNow support to activate entitlements remotely

explanation.correct: On-premise instances don't download entitlements automatically. You use the sn_ham_active_entitlements system property with comma-separated values like: ham_computer_license, ham_server_license, etc.

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is no entitlement file upload mechanism; the system property is used for on-premise instances.
HAM entitlements are managed via the system property, not the Software Entitlement table.
ServiceNow support doesn't activate on-premise entitlements; the system property is used.

questions.question: What happens to child assets when expenses are tracked in the TCO system?

options.text: Child asset expenses are tracked independently and do not affect the parent
Expenses on child assets are added to the TCO of the parent asset; removing a child doesn't affect parent TCO
Child asset expenses replace the parent asset expenses
Expenses are only tracked at the parent level and distributed to children

explanation.correct: When cost is incurred on a child asset, the same cost is added to the parent asset's TCO. If a child asset is removed, its expense lines persist and the parent's TCO is not affected. If a child is swapped, one expense line is created for operational cost.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Child expenses DO affect the parent — they are added to the parent's TCO.
Child expenses are added to the parent, they don't replace parent expenses.
Expenses can be tracked at both parent and child levels; child expenses roll up to the parent.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of lines that can be created in a Multiple model hardware asset refresh request?

explanation.correct: When using the Multiple model refresh type, you can create up to 50 lines, each specifying a different replacement model for a specific old asset.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The limit is 50 lines, not 25.
The limit is 50 lines, not 100.
There is a limit of 50 lines per multiple model refresh request.
